headline: US Civil Rights Division chief Harmeet Dhillon resigns following midterm elections
standfirst: Harmeet Dhillon has stepped down as head of the US Justice Department's Civil Rights Division. Her departure follows Democratic midterm victories and upcoming congressional inquiries into agency operations.
keyPoints: Harmeet Dhillon has resigned after 18 months leading the US Justice Department's Civil Rights Division.
Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the departure following Democratic victories in the US midterm elections.
The resignation precedes planned congressional probes into ICE fatal shootings and Jeffrey Epstein records.
Dhillon faced prior criticism from former department officials and lawmakers over her leadership and policy decisions.

paragraphs: The head of the United States Department of Justice civil rights division, Harmeet Dhillon, has resigned from her position after eighteen months in office. United States Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the departure on Thursday through a message published on social media. Dhillon is the first high-ranking official to step down from President Donald Trump's administration following the recent national midterm elections.

Her resignation comes immediately after the Democratic Party secured control of both chambers of the United States Congress. The incoming legislative majority has indicated plans to initiate broad congressional inquiries into several sensitive administrative matters. These upcoming probes are expected to focus heavily on how federal officials handled law enforcement actions and sensitive government documentation.

The Department of Justice referred inquiries regarding the precise timing of her resignation letter to the public statement made by the attorney general. The White House did not immediately offer official comment regarding the administrative transition. Dhillon had led the division responsible for enforcing federal anti-discrimination legislation since early 2025.

sections.heading: Leadership and division changes
paragraphs: Dhillon was formally confirmed by the Senate as Assistant Attorney General in April 2025. During her eighteen-month tenure, she directed a major restructuring of the civil rights division responsible for defending constitutional protections across the nation. Her appointment brought substantial shifts to the internal operations and priorities of the federal enforcement unit.

The restructuring efforts drew significant opposition from former federal legal personnel and government staff. In December 2025, hundreds of former Department of Justice employees signed an open letter expressing severe criticism over the management of the division. Opponents claimed that the reforms significantly damaged the agency's primary mission of combating systemic discrimination.

sections.heading: Congressional scrutiny and statements
paragraphs: Representative Robert Garcia, a California Democrat expected to chair the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, announced plans on Wednesday for four major investigations. The planned inquiries target potential abuses of authority within federal law enforcement agencies as well as administrative handling of unreleased government files. Congressional leaders have emphasised their intention to hold senior officials accountable for past decision-making.

Following the resignation announcement, Attorney General Todd Blanche praised the departing official's public service on social media. He stated that Dhillon had "enforced the law without fear or favor" throughout her period leading the civil rights division. Supporters of the administration maintain that her tenure successfully upheld federal standards across the country.

sections.heading: Controversies over federal probes
paragraphs: Controversy during Dhillon's leadership centered in part on decisions regarding fatal shootings involving federal agents. Earlier this year, reports indicated that she informed staff her division would not investigate the deaths of two American citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti. Both individuals were fatally shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel in Minneapolis, drawing widespread public attention.

Additionally, lawmakers raised questions regarding the handling of sensitive records linked to the Jeffrey Epstein investigation. During a closed-door hearing involving former Attorney General Pam Bondi, Garcia alleged that Dhillon repeatedly intervened to block questions about executive links to the file disclosures. Critics accused officials of shielding the administration from legislative oversight during those proceedings.

sections.heading: Next steps for Congress and DOJ
paragraphs: The transition comes as key House oversight committees prepare to conduct comprehensive investigations in the coming months. With Democrats taking control of both legislative chambers, oversight of executive agencies is expected to intensify dramatically. Federal lawmakers will review internal decision-making processes regarding the handling of agent-involved fatalities and sensitive government archives.

The Department of Justice has not yet announced a successor to lead the civil rights division following Dhillon's departure. The leadership change leaves a key administrative vacancy as the department faces mounting legislative scrutiny. Congressional leaders maintain that their planned inquiries will proceed regardless of personnel changes within the administration.

highlight: Dhillon is the first high-ranking official to step down from President Donald Trump's administration following the recent national midterm elections.

timeline.what: Harmeet Dhillon is confirmed as Assistant Attorney General leading the Civil Rights Division.
Hundreds of former Justice Department staff sign an open letter criticizing reforms within the Civil Rights Division.
Democrats win control of both chambers of the US Congress in midterm elections.
Representative Robert Garcia announces plans for major congressional investigations into executive oversight.
Attorney General Todd Blanche confirms Harmeet Dhillon's resignation.

socialSummary: Harmeet Dhillon resigns as head of the US Civil Rights Division ahead of planned congressional probes into ICE shootings and Epstein files.
